lines.japanese:
「そうですか！
美穂子、卒業決まったんだ…」
lines.english: “Really? Mihoko’s going to graduate?”

lines.japanese:
「ええ、先週、先生方とご相談して…
出席日数は少し足りないけれど、
二学期の成績は問題なかったから特例ってことで」
lines.english: “Yes. We spoke to her teachers last week. She was a little short on attendance, but her second-term grades were fine, so they agreed to make an exception.”

lines.japanese: 「よかった…よかったぁ」
lines.english: “Thank goodness… Oh, thank goodness.”

lines.japanese:
「ありがとう。これも杉浦さんのおかげよ。
あの子が休んでる間も、
いつもノート届けてくれてたから」
lines.english: “Thank you. You helped make this possible, Sugiura. Even while she was out, you kept bringing her your notes.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、わたしなんか…」
lines.english: “No, I barely did anything…”

lines.japanese:
「これで、とりあえずは一息ついたってところね。
…まだまだ解決できていない問題は多いけれど」
lines.english: “At least we can breathe easy for a moment. …There are still so many things we haven’t resolved.”

lines.japanese:
「それで今日は？
美穂子にも内緒で、私に話したいことって…？」
lines.english: “So, what brings you here today? You said there was something you wanted to discuss without Mihoko knowing…”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、実は…」
lines.english: “Yes. The thing is…”

lines.japanese: 「お水お代わりいかがですか？」
lines.english: “Can I top up your water?”

lines.japanese: 「しぃぃぃぃ～！」
lines.english: “Shhhhhhh!”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい…失礼いたしました」
lines.english: “O-oh. I’m sorry…”

lines.japanese:
…ここで矢田さんのお母さんに、
後ろを振り返られると困る。
lines.english: The last thing I needed was for Mihoko’s mother to turn around.

lines.japanese: 何しろ、二度ほどご挨拶させてもらったことあるし。
lines.english: I’d met her twice before. She would recognize me.

lines.japanese:
「その、解決できてない問題…
美穂子が進学しないって言い出した理由について、です」
lines.english: “It’s about one of those unresolved problems—why Mihoko says she isn’t going to college.”

lines.japanese:
「っ、知ってるのね？
よかった。あの子ったら今まで一言も話してくれなくて。
相変わらず微熱続きだから、強くも聞けなくて…」
lines.english: “You know why? Thank goodness. She hasn’t told us anything. And she still has a slight fever, so I haven’t been able to press her…”

lines.japanese: 「そう、ですか…」
lines.english: “I… see.”

lines.japanese:
「それでどうなの？
やっぱりクラスのお友達と
うまく行かなかったのかしら…」
lines.english: “So what happened? Was she having trouble getting along with her classmates after all…?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ええと、それは…」
lines.english: “Um… well…”

lines.japanese:
「あの子、中等部の頃はよく学校行きたくないって
口にしてて…付属に入ってからはそういうこと
言わなくなったから安心してたんだけど…」
lines.english: “Back in middle school, she was always saying she didn’t want to go. She stopped after she entered Houjou High, so I thought I could finally stop worrying…”

lines.japanese: そういえば、小春も言ってたっけ…
lines.english: Come to think of it, Koharu had told me the same thing…

lines.japanese:
幼稚園からの純粋培養の峰城生なのに、
あまりクラスに溶け込めていなかったって。
lines.english: Mihoko was Houjou through and through—she’d been there since kindergarten—and still had never quite found her place in the class.

lines.japanese:
「それも杉浦さんが朝迎えに来てくれたり、
いつも仲良くしてくれたからだったのよ。
本当に感謝してるの」
lines.english: “That changed because you came for her every morning and stayed such a good friend to her. I really am grateful.”

lines.japanese:
「っ、ごめんなさい！
でも、今回の原因は、わたしなんです！」
lines.english: “I’m sorry! But this time, I’m the reason she’s like this!”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
「わたしが、美穂子のこと傷つけちゃったんです。
だから、美穂子にとって今までよりも深刻なんです」
lines.english: “I hurt her. And because it was me, this is worse for her than anything that happened before.”

lines.japanese:
「おばさんの言う通り、
わたしと美穂子、仲良かったと思います」
lines.english: “You’re right, Mrs. Yada. Mihoko and I were close.”

lines.japanese:
「美穂子、わたしのこと一番信用してくれてたって、
うぬぼれじゃなく、そう思ってました」
lines.english: “I honestly believed she trusted me more than anyone. I don’t think I was flattering myself.”

lines.japanese:
「そんなわたしが…あのコを裏切ったから、
だから、今まで以上に
誰にも心を開いてくれないんだと思います」
lines.english: “Then I betrayed her. I think that’s why she’s shut everyone out even more completely than before.”

lines.japanese: 「…何があったの？」
lines.english: “…What happened between you?”

lines.japanese: 「それは…言えません」
lines.english: “I can’t tell you that.”

lines.japanese:
「ただ言えることは…
何十年も生きてきた大人の人たちには、
もしかしたら、馬鹿みたいでくだらないこと…」
lines.english: “All I can say is… to adults with decades behind them, it may look stupid. Trivial.”

lines.japanese:
「けれど、たった十数年しか生きてないわたしたちには、
何よりも大事な問題です」
lines.english: “But we’re still teenagers. We haven’t even lived two decades. To us, nothing could matter more.”

lines.japanese: 「そう…そうなの」
lines.english: “I see… Yes. I understand.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “I’m sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、そのことを話してくれただけで…」
lines.english: “No. Telling me even that much is…”

lines.japanese:
「それで、さらに厚かましいお願いなんですけど…
おばさんに、頼みたいことがあるんです」
lines.english: “And after telling you all that, I have an even more presumptuous favor to ask…”

lines.japanese: 「何かしら？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「わたし、美穂子と話がしたいんです」
lines.english: “I want to talk to Mihoko.”

lines.japanese: 「それは…家に来るということ？」
lines.english: “You mean… you want to come to the house?”

lines.japanese:
「いえ、今直接話をしても、こじれるだけだと思います。
だからこれ…渡して欲しいんです」
lines.english: “No. If I try to speak to her now, I’ll only make things worse. So… I want you to give her this.”
“A letter?”

lines.japanese:
「今のわたしの気持ち、全部書きました。
感情的にならずに、落ち着いて、よく考えて…
けど正直に、隠し事なしで、いいことも悪いことも」
lines.english: “I put everything I feel into it. I kept my head, thought it through, and wrote honestly—no secrets. The good and the bad.”

lines.japanese:
「…美穂子に渡せばいいのね？
わかったわ」
lines.english: “…You want me to give this to Mihoko? All right.”

lines.japanese:
「そんな安請け合いしていいことじゃないと思いますよ？
美穂子、本当にわたしのこと許してないから」
lines.english: “You shouldn’t promise that so easily. Mihoko really hasn’t forgiven me.”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ、絶対に渡します」
lines.english: “No. I’m giving it to her. I promise.”

lines.japanese: 「でも…」
lines.english: “But…”

lines.japanese:
「こうしてお友達が一生懸命に話しかけてくれてるのに、
それでも応えないとしたら、それは美穂子の方が悪いわ」
lines.english: “A friend is trying this hard to reach her. If Mihoko still refuses to answer, then Mihoko is the one in the wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「おばさん…」
lines.english: “Mrs. Yada…”

lines.japanese:
「…でも、あの子がそうなってしまった理由は、
わたしたちが甘やかしたせいなのかもしれないけど」
lines.english: “…Though maybe she only became this way because we spoiled her.”

lines.japanese:
「そんなこと…ないです。
美穂子、本当にいいコです。
わたしがいけないんです」
lines.english: “No, that isn’t it. Mihoko really is a wonderful person. I’m the one who did wrong.”

lines.japanese:
「…とにかくこの手紙は、
わたしが責任持って預かります。
そして、必ず美穂子に読ませるようにします」
lines.english: “In any case, leave the letter with me. I’ll take responsibility for it. And I will make sure Mihoko reads it.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、ございます」
lines.english: “Thank you… so much.”

lines.japanese:
「いいえ、こちらこそありがとう。
そして、改めてお願いします。
…これからも美穂子と仲良くしてあげてね？」
lines.english: “No, thank you. And let me ask you one more time… Please keep being Mihoko’s friend.”

lines.japanese: 「………頑張りますっ」
lines.english: “…I’ll do everything I can.”

lines.japanese: 「お疲れ」
lines.english: “You survived.”

lines.japanese: 「はぁぁぁぁ～」
lines.english: “Haaaaaaaaah…”

lines.japanese:
矢田さんのお母さんが去り、
代わりに目の前に俺が座った途端、
小春は全身を使って大きな息を吐き出した。
lines.english: The moment Mihoko’s mother left and I slid into the seat across from her, Koharu exhaled with her entire body.

lines.japanese:
ま、喧嘩した友達の母親に、
そのことを正直に話すというのは、
ちょっとばかり勇気のいることだったかもしれないな。
lines.english: Apparently, admitting to your friend’s mother that the two of you had fallen out took a little courage.

lines.japanese: 「読んでくれるかな？　美穂子…」
lines.english: “Do you think Mihoko will read it?”

lines.japanese:
「読むさ。
お母さんがあれだけ太鼓判を押したんだ。
きっと粘り強く話してくれるよ」
lines.english: “She will. Her mother gave us her word. She’ll keep working on Mihoko until she listens.”

lines.japanese: 「それでも、許してくれなかったら…」
lines.english: “What if she reads it and still won’t forgive me?”

lines.japanese:
「そのためにお母さんを
味方に引き入れたんじゃないか」
lines.english: “That’s why we got her mother on our side.”

lines.japanese: 「…どういう意味です？」
lines.english: “…What do you mean?”

lines.japanese:
「これで俺たちは、いついかなるときでも、
矢田さんに手紙を渡せるようになったんだぞ？
何度でも、何度でも…」
lines.english: “Now we can get a letter to Mihoko whenever we need to. Again and again, for as long as it takes.”

lines.japanese: 「先輩…」
lines.english: “Haruki…”

lines.japanese:
「長期戦だって視野に入れてる。
抜かりはないって」
lines.english: “I planned for the long haul. I told you—I’ve covered everything.”

lines.japanese: これが、俺が小春に授けた最後の作戦。
lines.english: That was the last strategy I had given Koharu.

lines.japanese: 「本当に、色々考えてるんですね。大人の手口」
lines.english: “You really do think of everything. Such grown-up tactics.”
“…Well. Yes.”

lines.japanese:
王道かつ本道な手だと思うんだけど、
様々なリスクを考慮する計算高さが、
いつも直球勝負の小春にはどうにも卑怯に映るらしかった。
lines.english: I thought it was the obvious, aboveboard move. Apparently, accounting for every possible risk still looked underhanded to Koharu, who only knew how to throw straight fastballs.

lines.japanese:
…“彼女”にもこの計算高さが通用してたら、
俺たちはもうちょっと楽に生きて行けたのかな…
lines.english: If that kind of calculation had ever worked on ‘her,’ maybe we all could’ve lived a little more easily…

lines.japanese: 「でも、どうしてあんなに自信満々だったんですか？」
lines.english: “But why were you so sure it would work?”

lines.japanese: 「なにが？」
lines.english: “About what?”

lines.japanese:
「お母さんを味方につけるって作戦のことです。
絶対にうまく行くって言ってましたよね？」
lines.english: “The plan to win her mother over. You said it couldn’t fail.”

lines.japanese:
「そりゃ…矢田さんのことを誰よりも心配してて、
誰よりも愛してる人だから」
lines.english: “Because no one worries about Mihoko more than her mother does. And no one loves her more.”

lines.japanese:
「小春には失礼かもしれないけど、
それこそ、小春よりも、な」
lines.english: “No offense, but she loves Mihoko even more than you do.”

lines.japanese:
「…それほど知ってる訳じゃないのに、
よくそこまで信じ切ることができますね」
lines.english: “…You barely know her. How can you trust her that completely?”

lines.japanese: 「………信じてなかったよ」
lines.english: “…I didn’t use to.”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
「母親って人種を、一人しか知らなかった頃は、
まるっきり信じてなかった」
lines.english: “Back when I only knew one specimen of the species called ‘mother,’ I didn’t trust them at all.”
“Haruki…?”

lines.japanese:
「けど、色んな相手と付き合っていくとさ、
色んな人の色んな母親を知る機会があってさ」
lines.english: “But the more people I got to know, the more chances I had to meet their mothers too.”

lines.japanese:
何しろ付属時代は、
ほとんどのクラスメイトの家を訪問したことがあり、
そのせいで、ほとんどの母親と話をした。
lines.english: Back at Houjou High, I’d been to nearly every classmate’s house. Which meant I’d spoken to nearly every classmate’s mother.

lines.japanese:
武也の母親は、結構セレブっぽい人で、
依緒の母親は、逆に完全な下町っ子で。
lines.english: Takeya’s mother had the air of a socialite. Io’s was the exact opposite: a downtown girl through and through.

lines.japanese:
そして…
どんな事でも娘と話し合う、本当に裏表のない母親と。
lines.english: There was one mother who spoke openly with her daughter about absolutely everything…

lines.japanese:
誤解や性格の不一致が重なってずっと絶縁してたけど、
結局、娘が可愛くてしょうがなかった母親と。
lines.english: And another who had spent years estranged from her daughter through misunderstanding and clashing personalities, but ultimately loved her beyond reason.

lines.japanese: 「…多数決で、信じてもいいかなって思うようになった」
lines.english: “…Put it to a majority vote, and I decided mothers might be worth trusting after all.”

lines.japanese:
色んな『母親という生き物』に接していくうちに、
いつの間にか、賭けてみる気になれていた。
lines.english: Somewhere in the course of meeting so many examples of the creature known as ‘mother,’ I’d become willing to take the gamble.

lines.japanese:
「さっきの小春との会話を聞いてますます確信した。
いいお母さんだよな」
lines.english: “Listening to her talk to you just confirmed it. She’s a good mother.”

lines.japanese:
「少なくとも、美穂子やわたしよりは
話のわかる人ですよ？」
lines.english: “At the very least, she’s more reasonable than either Mihoko or me.”

lines.japanese:
「お前らも、片方でもいいからあのくらい柔軟だったら、
こんなことにはならなかったかもな」
lines.english: “If even one of you had been that flexible, maybe none of this would’ve happened.”

lines.japanese: 「ですね、ふふ…」
lines.english: “I suppose not. Heh…”

lines.japanese: それか、俺がそうだったなら…
lines.english: Or if I had been…

lines.japanese:
なんて、やめとこう。
後悔してももう遅いから、
前に進むって決めたんだっけ、俺たちは。
lines.english: No. Enough. It was too late for regret. We’d already decided to move forward.

lines.japanese:
「ね、先輩。
さっきの話…」
lines.english: “Um… about what you said earlier…”

lines.japanese: 「…さっきのって？」
lines.english: “…Which part?”

lines.japanese:
「えっと、その…
先輩の、お母さんのこと…」
lines.english:
“Well, I was wondering…
about your mother…”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「小春？」
lines.english: “Koharu?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、なんでもないです。
lines.english: “No, never mind. It’s…

lines.japanese: …わたしが聞いていいことじゃないから」
lines.english: …not something I have the right to ask.”

lines.japanese: 「…そうか」
lines.english: “…I see.”

lines.japanese:
もじもじと俯く小春らしくない小春に、
俺は、何も考えていない風に首をひねってみせる。
lines.english: Koharu fidgeted with her eyes down—so unlike herself. I tilted my head and played innocent.

lines.japanese:
本当は聞こえてたけど、
小春自身が『聞いていいことじゃない』と思ってる限り、
まだ、聞こえないふりをした方がいい。
lines.english: I’d heard her perfectly well. But as long as she believed she had no right to ask, I thought it better to pretend I hadn’t.

lines.japanese:
「ね、先輩。
お昼も近いし、ここでご飯食べちゃいましょうか？」
lines.english: “It’s almost lunchtime. Why don’t we eat here?”

lines.japanese:
「ああ、そうだな。
で、そのまま部屋に戻って勉強再開ってことで」
lines.english: “Sure. Then straight back to my place, and we get back to work.”

lines.japanese:
とにかく、これで俺の種まきは全て終わった。
後は、芽が出るのを待つだけ。
lines.english: With that, I’d planted every seed I could. Now all I could do was wait for them to sprout.

lines.japanese:
もちろんその間に、一生懸命水をまき、肥料を与え、
大きく育ってくれと祈らないといけないけど…
lines.english: Not passively, of course. I still had to water them, fertilize them, and pray they grew strong…

lines.japanese: でも、これでやれることは全部やった。
lines.english: But I had done everything there was to do.

lines.japanese: …ただ一つを除いて。
lines.english: Everything except one thing.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、ちょっと休憩にするか」
lines.english: “Why don’t we take a break?”

lines.japanese:
「それとも、今日はもう終わりにするか？
一応、予定してたところまでは進んだし」
lines.english: “Or do you want to stop for today? We made it through everything I had planned.”

lines.japanese: 「小春？」
lines.english: “Koharu?”
“…Oh, come on.”

lines.japanese:
マンツーマンの冬期講習も、
今日で５日目。
lines.english: Day five of our one-on-one winter crash course.

lines.japanese:
ここで朝から晩まで１２時間。
家に帰ってからも俺の出した宿題をこなすのに６時間。
lines.english: Twelve hours here, morning to night. Then six more at home, doing the homework I assigned.

lines.japanese:
家からここまでの往復に１時間。
三回の食事と入浴で計２時間。
lines.english: One hour traveling there and back. Two hours total for three meals and a bath.

lines.japanese:
そして残りの３時間で睡眠…と行かず、
それすら削って少しでもノルマ超えを果たそうとすれば…
lines.english: That should have left three hours for sleep. Except she carved pieces out of those too, trying to beat the quota by even a little…

lines.japanese: 「………すぅぅ…ぅぅ」
lines.english: “…Hhhh… hhh…”

lines.japanese: 当然、いずれこうなる。
lines.english: Sooner or later, this was inevitable.

lines.japanese: ほんと、加減を知らない奴だからなぁ。
lines.english: She genuinely had no idea how to pace herself.

lines.japanese:
「おい、起きろ。
そろそろ終電の時間だぞ？」
lines.english: “Hey. Wake up. It’s almost time for the last train.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　んぅ…」
lines.english: “Hm…? Mmm…”

lines.japanese:
見事なまでに机に突っ伏して、
いくら肩を揺すろうが、起きる気配が感じられない。
lines.english: She had folded over the desk with impressive thoroughness. No matter how I shook her shoulder, she showed no sign of waking.

lines.japanese:
「小春、小春…
ったく、風邪ひくぞ」
lines.english: “Koharu. Koharu… Come on. You’ll catch cold.”

lines.japanese:
なんて嘆いてみせるのは、
実はちょっとした詭弁で…
lines.english: But if I was honest, that was a pretty flimsy excuse…

lines.japanese:
本気で起こそうとする力が、
俺の手に込められてないのは明らかだった。
lines.english: I plainly wasn’t putting anything like enough force into it to wake her.

lines.japanese: 「ふ～…んぅぅぅぅ～」
lines.english: “Hhhh… mmmmm…”

lines.japanese:
穏やかで規則的な寝息を聞きながら、
その『眠ってるときは可愛いのに』と言うには
普段から可愛い寝顔を覗き込む。
lines.english: Her breathing was soft and steady. I leaned in for a better look. I wished I could say she was only cute when she slept. Unfortunately, she was cute all the time.

lines.japanese:
肩を揺すっていたはずの手は、
いつの間にか、その指に小春の髪を絡めてた。
lines.english: The hand that was supposed to be shaking her shoulder had somehow ended up winding strands of her hair around its fingers.

lines.japanese: 「すぅぅ…すぅ…」
lines.english: “Hhhh… hhhh…”

lines.japanese:
堕ちた俺を引き上げようと手を伸ばし、
俺に引きずり落とされてしまった小春。
lines.english: Koharu had reached out to pull me back up after my fall. I had grabbed that hand and dragged her down with me.

lines.japanese: 穢れた俺を救おうとして、穢れてしまった小春。
lines.english: She had tried to save me from my own corruption, and I had corrupted her in turn.

lines.japanese: 俺に、汚されてしまった小春。
lines.english: I was the one who had defiled her.

lines.japanese:
それなのに…
心も身体も、ボロボロに傷つけられたはずなのに…
lines.english: And yet… though I must have torn both her heart and her body to pieces…

lines.japanese: 「ん、んぅ…ふぅぅ…」
lines.english: “Mm… mmm… hhhh…”

lines.japanese:
なんで、こうして白いままでいられるんだよ…
綺麗なままの寝顔、俺に見せてくれるんだよ…
lines.english: how could she still look so clean, so white? How could she look this beautiful in her sleep?

lines.japanese:
…抱きしめたくて、
その衝動を抑えなくちゃならない方の身にもなってくれ。
lines.english: Seriously. Spare a thought for the man who had to stop himself from pulling you into his arms.

lines.japanese: 「ふぅん…ん…んぅぅ…」
lines.english: “Hhh… mm… mmmm…”

lines.japanese:
あの、前に進むって決めた日以来、
小春は、以前みたいに発作的に泣くことはなくなった。
lines.english: Since the day we decided to move forward, Koharu had stopped breaking into sudden tears the way she used to.

lines.japanese:
今、自分がしていることを信じてるのか。
それとも、俺を信じてくれてるのか…
lines.english: Did she believe in what she was doing? Or did she believe in me…?

lines.japanese: 「小春」
lines.english: “Koharu.”

lines.japanese:
なんて強い奴だ、なんて凄い奴だ。
羨ましい、妬ましい。
lines.english: God, she was strong. Incredible. I envied her for it. I was jealous of her for it.

lines.japanese: そして…いとおしい。
lines.english: And… I loved her.

lines.japanese: 「小春…」
lines.english: “Koharu…”

lines.japanese: 報いないと。
lines.english: I had to give her something in return.

lines.japanese:
この一生懸命な少女が、
自分の努力に見合う幸せを掴めるように。
lines.english: This girl was giving everything she had. She deserved every bit of happiness all that effort could earn her.

lines.japanese:
「そろそろ起きるんだ。
…今は、泊まらないって約束だろ？」
lines.english: “Time to wake up. …We promised you wouldn’t stay the night for now, remember?”

lines.japanese: 「ふぇ…ぇ？」
lines.english: “Huh…?”

lines.japanese: そしていつか俺も。
lines.english: And maybe, someday, I could too.

lines.japanese:
少女の眩しさを辛いと感じなくなり、
目を背けず、見つめ返せるようになれたなら…
lines.english: If someday her radiance stopped hurting to look at—if I could meet her gaze without turning away…
